messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — Ava Retail pilot

Hi Ava — great to meet earlier. Quick post-call recap and next steps from our side: 

- Recap: You’re interested in a 3-month pilot to validate inference economics for your personalization API (session-based prompts + short user histories). Target model family: LLaMA-variant (we discussed 13B / 7B quantized variants).
- Ask: Could you confirm expected token volumes (monthly and peak qps), and an initial target budget range for the pilot? That helps me lock down unit economics.
- Our assumptions to validate: continuous batching will capture ~60-80% effective batching on your steady stream; peak concurrency (burst) might see 20-50 concurrent requests.
- Next steps: 1) You share a representative 24-72 hour traffic sample (timestamps + tokens/request), 2) We send preliminary $/1M token ranges and a recommended batching/concurrency config, 3) Sync to agree SLOs and kickoff pilot.

I’ve attached the post-call deck with the mutual action plan. To give you something immediate: what’s your current ballpark for tokens/month and target $/1M tokens (e.g., $300-$800)? Even a rough range is helpful.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for formal pricing once we have token numbers.

— Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya — great recap. A few quick answers from our side:

- Monthly volumes: targeting 50M tokens/month for the pilot (roughly 1.7M tokens/day).
- Peak patterns: steady background traffic (authentication / personalization lookups) ~25 qps steady, with ~3x bursts during promo windows (peaks up to ~75 qps for ~30-60 minutes).
- Token distribution: median request ~120 tokens, 90th percentile ~300 tokens. Many requests are short (20–60 tokens) but we have a long-tail of multi-turn sessions for power users.
- Budget: we’re aiming for a pilot budget in the $20k–$30k/month range for infra + service. Open to adjusting if the unit economics make sense.

I can share a 72-hour log export (anonymized) — sending to your shared Drive link now. Also looping in procurement for any intake forms.

Best,
Ava

ava@avaretail.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Ava Retail pilot

Thanks Ava — that’s exactly the shape of data we need. Quick follow-up on unit economics so Marissa can prepare a pricing worksheet: 

- Baseline assumptions to price: model variant (7B quant vs 13B quant), expected effective continuous batching capture (we use prefix + KV cache for sessions), and concurrency.
- If we assume 50M tokens/month and an effective batching capture of 70% (i.e., 70% of tokens benefit from batching gains), and target pilot budget $25k/month, that implies a target blended price of ~$500 / 1M tokens.
- Ballpark ranges we typically see: $250–$900 / 1M tokens depending on model size, quantization, and how much continuous batching reduces per-token GPU work.

For Marissa / Camila: can you run a quick calc for 50M tokens/month under two scenarios: (A) 7B quant with 70% batching capture, (B) 13B quant with 60% batching capture. Include an estimated range for concurrency handling costs assuming sustained 25 qps steady + 3x peaks to 75 qps.

Ava — if you can confirm whether end-to-end latency SLO needs to be <200ms p50 or if 300–400ms is acceptable during peaks, that will shift recommended instance sizing/overprovisioning.

I’ve attached a quick pricing_estimate.csv with the fields we’ll fill out.

— Aditya
Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Ava Retail pilot

On Thu, Apr 15, 2027 at 1:20 PM Aditya Rao wrote:
> For Marissa / Camila: can you run a quick calc for 50M tokens/month under two scenarios: (A) 7B quant with 70% batching capture, (B) 13B quant with 60% batching capture. Include an estimated range for concurrency handling costs assuming sustained 25 qps steady + 3x peaks to 75 qps.

Quick set of numbers (very high level; will refine after we ingest the 72-hour sample):

Scenario A — 7B quant (70% continuous batching):
- Effective tokens billed (work-equivalent): ~0.55x raw tokens after batching efficiencies -> work = 27.5M work-tokens equivalent
- Infra + service blended cost range: $220–$420 per 1M raw tokens -> at 50M tokens that’s $11k–$21k/mo
- With margins and support, list/pricing to customer typically lands at $320–$520 / 1M tokens

Scenario B — 13B quant (60% continuous batching):
- Effective tokens billed: ~0.7x -> work = 35M work-tokens equivalent
- Infra + service blended cost range: $350–$700 per 1M raw tokens -> at 50M tokens that’s $17.5k–$35k/mo
- List/pricing to customer typically $480–$820 / 1M tokens

Concurrency note: to hit <200ms p50 we’d need modest headroom for peaks — recommend autoscale buffer for sustained 25 qps + 3x peaks; this increases effective infra cost ~10–20% depending on buffer policy. If 300–400ms is acceptable, we can reduce overprovisioning and unit price improves ~8–12%.

Recommendation to align with Ava’s $20–30k budget: start pilot on 7B quant profile with optimized continuous batching (expected blended price target ~$350–$450 / 1M tokens), monitor quality regression and move to 13B for higher quality if needed.

I’ll prepare a short pricing worksheet and a sample SLO config.

— Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ava Thompson <ava@avaretail.com>

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — Ava Retail pilot

Thanks everyone — this is very helpful and aligns with our expectations. A few confirmations: 

- We’ll proceed with the pilot scoped at 50M tokens/month. Target budget: $25k/month.
- Preference: start on 7B quant (lower per-token cost) with an agreed quality checklist to validate output; if we need higher fidelity we’ll evaluate a switch to 13B in month 2.
- Latency SLO: 300ms p50 acceptable; spikes tolerated up to 500ms during 30–60 minute promo windows.
- We’ll upload the 72-hour anonymized sample to the Drive link you shared and procurement will fill out the intake. I’ve attached the procurement form for your legal team.

Next step: can we schedule a kickoff + technical runbook review next Wed (Apr 21) at 10am PT?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — excited to get this started.

— Ava
